source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn flea beetle (ទាកគូពោត, Corn Flea Beetle): the flea beetle is a very small insect that lives, as its name suggests, mostly on corn plants; there are many species, some living specifically on corn. Damage is often seen on corn plants that are about 10-20 days old. Adults have two brownish wing covers, one with a yellow-ish stripe/spot pattern on top; adults have wing length of about 1.5-3 mm. This insect causes damage by chewing/rasping and sucking on plant tissue.

This beetle can be found on both leaves and stems, feeding in a scraping/piercing pattern, and is at particular risk of building up on plants about 4-5 days to a week old, at 5-6 mm plant size, which then dries out during about 25 days old, corresponding to leaf yellowing/browning.

Control and prevention measures similar to those used for other similar pests: keep the field clean of weeds and remove residues that could harbor the pest, particularly near stored clean seed; collect infected debris; ensure proper drainage before planting; and irrigate at an efficient rate that can help suppress flea beetle populations by washing them off leaves, since drought conditions in the field can favor their build-up.
